questions.q_en: Select the grammatically correct sentence.
options_en: The company has invested a large amount of money in new machineries.
The company has invested a large amount of money in new machinery.
The company has invested a large number of money in new machinery.
The company has invested a large number of money in new machineries.
questions.solution_en:
The correct answer is option b).

Explanation: "Machinery" is an uncountable noun and hence, cannot have a plural form. So, "machineries" is incorrect. This makes options a) and d) incorrect.

Additionally, "amount" is used with uncountable nouns like "money," while "number" is used with countable nouns. This makes option c) incorrect.

Note: Countable and uncountable nouns: 1. Countable nouns are the class of nouns that can be counted, for example, 'table' - one table, two tables, three tables, etc. 2. Uncountable nouns are the nouns that cannot be counted or usually are not counted, for example, light, water, milk, information, furniture, etc. They do not generally have a plural form and can't be preceded by 'a' or 'an'. Many abstract nouns are typically uncountable. Some uncountable nouns can be used in the plural as well, depending on the meaning or context of the word.

Plastic bags are difficult to recycle due to their lightweight (3) ________, which causes them to clog machinery in recycling facilities. Each year, millions of tons of plastic waste enter the oceans, posing a (4) __________ threat to marine ecosystems. As a result, many recycling programs do not accept plastic bags, leading to more waste in (5) ________.

questions.solution_en:

These blockages can prevent the proper digestion and absorption of food, which would lead to starvation. This makes "starvation" the most appropriate word to complete the sentence meaningfully and logically. Other words do not relate to the consequences of ingesting plastic.

Hence, option (b) is correct.

Given below are six sentences, out of which sentences A and F are in correct position. Sentences B, C, D, E are in jumbled order. Select the option that gives the correct order.

A. There was nothing greater than the sound of a whistle from a kettle to start the day.

B. That day was no exception.

C. She would wear the same colour clothing every day and would follow the same daily routine.

D. It was the first sound that Ms. Mary would wake up to every morning.

E. She was a simple woman both in spirit and fashion.

F. She went down to the kitchen where she made her cup of chai tea with two sugars.
questions.solution_en:

C also states that she would follow the same routine every day. B follows C as it refers back to A and D and builds up on them. Sentence F is the last sentence. Therefore, ADECBF becomes the correct order among the given options.

Hence, option (c) is the correct answer.

Option c) gest is an archaic noun meaning a notable deed or exploit, or a story of such. It is not a verb and is contextually incorrect.

Option d) quest is a noun, meaning a long or arduous search for something. While one might be on a quest for an answer, "quest" itself is not the verb for finding it in this structure.

So, the complete sentence is: He guessed the correct answer to the riddle after thinking for a while.

Hence, option (b) is the correct answer.

questions.solution_en:
The sentence in the Direct Speech is in Simple Present Tense. Therefore, the sentence in the Indirect Speech should be in Simple Past Tense.

Simple Present (Subject + V1 + Object) should be converted into Simple Past (Subject +V2 + Object).

"That" is used in place of Inverted Commas while transforming the sentence from Direct Speech to Indirect Speech.

For example:

He said, "I never go to the village." (Direct Speech)

He said that he never went to the village. (Indirect Speech)

The following things in the sentence should change when changed from Direct speech to Indirect Speech:

To convert the direct speech "I am determined..." into reported speech, the pronoun "I" changes to "she" (assuming the scientist is female, as implied by options), and the verb tense shifts back (present "am" to past "was").

Therefore, the correct answer is:

The correct sentence is: "The scientist confidently asserted that she was determined to publish her findings."

questions.q_en:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in direct speech.

Fiona enquired whether I had gone to school on Tuesday.
options_en: "Had you been going to school on Tuesday?" Fiona asked me.
"Where are you going on Tuesday?'' Fiona asked me.
"Did you go to school on Tuesday?'' Fiona asked me.
"Are you gone to school on Tuesday? Fiona enquired.
questions.solution_en:
In the case of Interrogative sentences like this, "enquired (of)", "wanted to know", "enquired", etc. in Indirect Speech is changed into "said/asked" in Direct Speech. In Direct speech, the verb is always placed before the subject, unlike in Indirect Speech. If there is a question whose answer can come as "Yes" or "No", we remove the inverted commas and add the conjunction "If" or "Whether" in the Indirect Speech and the verb/s "Is/are/am/was/were" before the subject, in Direct Speech.

For example:

Ravi asked me if she was studying. (Indirect Speech)

Ravi said to me, "Is she studying?" (Direct Speech)

The sentence in the Indirect Speech is in Past Perfect Tense.

There are three cases when the Indirect Speech is in Past Perfect Tense.

I. Tense remains the same.

II. Past perfect changes to Present Perfect

III. Past perfect changes to Simple Past

Case 1: Past Perfect (Subject + had + V3 + Object) tense will be kept intact.

For example:

He said that he had just finished the movie. (Indirect Speech)

He said, "I had just finished the movie" (Direct Speech)

Case 2: Past Perfect (Subject + had + V3 +Object) will be converted into Present Perfect (Subject + has/have + V3+Object).

For example:

He said that he had got a new job. (Indirect Speech)

He said, "I have got a new job." (Direct Speech)

Case 3: Past Perfect (Subject + had+ V3 + Object) will be converted into Past Simple (Subject + V2 + Object).

For example:

He said that Arya had sent him a book. (Indirect Speech)

He said, "Arya sent me a book" (Direct Speech). Here, case 3 will be used, as per the options.

The following things in the sentence will change when changed from Indirect Speech to Direct Speech:

Reporting verb 'enquired' changed to 'asked me'.

The verb phrase 'I had gone' changed to 'Did you go'.

Therefore, the correct answer is: (c).

questions.q_en:
Directions [Set of 4 Questions]: Read the given passage and answer the questions that follow.

Biomimicry, the practice of drawing inspiration from nature to solve human challenges, is revolutionizing modern engineering. Nature, through millions of years of evolution, has perfected designs that are energy-efficient, sustainable, and highly adaptable. Engineers are increasingly looking to the natural world to develop innovative solutions to complex problems, whether in architecture, manufacturing, or materials science.

One of the most famous examples of biomimicry is the development of Velcro. The idea came from Swiss engineer George de Mestral, who observed how burrs stuck to his dog's fur. By mimicking the hook-and-loop mechanism of the burrs, Mestral created a fastening system that is now widely used. Another key example is the design of energy-efficient buildings inspired by termite mounds. Termites construct their nests with natural ventilation systems that maintain a stable temperature, even in extreme heat. Inspired by this, architects have designed climate-responsive buildings that reduce the need for artificial heating or cooling, saving energy.

In materials science, the lotus leaf's ability to resist dirt and water has led to the development of self-cleaning surfaces. These surfaces use microstructures similar to those on the leaf, preventing the accumulation of dust or grime. Similarly, researchers are studying the structure of spider silk, which is both incredibly strong and lightweight, to create synthetic materials for use in everything from medical sutures to aerospace components.

Biomimicry offers more than just clever designs. It emphasizes the importance of sustainability. By mimicking nature's solutions, engineers can create technologies that work in harmony with the environment, reducing waste and conserving resources. As this field continues to grow, it promises a future where human innovation is increasingly aligned with the natural world.

Which example best illustrates how nature has inspired architectural innovation?
options_en: The creation of Velcro based on the hook-like structure of burrs.
The design of self-cleaning surfaces modelled after lotus leaves.
The development of buildings with natural ventilation inspired by termite mounds.
The production of lightweight synthetic materials based on spider silk.
questions.solution_en:
Refer to the following excerpt from the second paragraph - "Another key example is the design of energy-efficient buildings inspired by termite mounds. Termites construct their nests with natural ventilation systems that maintain a stable temperature, even in extreme heat. Inspired by this, architects have designed climate-responsive buildings that reduce the need for artificial heating or cooling, saving energy."

The passage describes how termites build nests with natural ventilation systems that maintain stable temperatures. Architects have used this principle to design buildings that regulate temperature without relying heavily on artificial heating or cooling. This is a clear case of biomimicry applied to architecture.

Hence, option (c) is the answer.

questions.q_en:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in reported speech.

John said, "I was studying for the exam last evening."
options_en: John said that he had studied for the exam the previous evening.
John said that he was studying for the exam the last evening.
John said that he is studying for the exam the previous evening.
John said that he had been studying for the exam the previous evening.
questions.solution_en:
The sentence in the Direct Speech is in Past Continuous Tense. Therefore, the sentence in the Indirect Speech should be in Past Perfect Continuous Tense.

Past Continuous (Subject + was/were + V1 + ing + Object) should be converted into Past Perfect Continuous (Subject + had + been + V1 + ing + Object).

For example:

He said, "I was watching television last night." (Direct Speech)

He said that he had been watching television the previous night. (Indirect Speech)

The following things in the sentence should change when changed from Direct speech to Indirect Speech:

'Said' is changed to 'said that'.

'I' is changed to 'he'.

'Was' is changed to 'had been'.

'Last evening' is changed to 'the previous night'.

Therefore, the correct answer is: John said that he had been studying for the exam the previous evening.

Hence, (d) is the correct answer.

questions.q_en:
The following sentence has an error in its tense. Identify the error and select the correct sentence from the options.

If you had apprised me about your problem earlier, I would have allow you to go.
options_en: If you had apprised me about your problem earlier, I would have allowed you to go.
If you apprised me about your problem earlier, I would have allowed you to go.
If you had apprised me about your problem earlier, I would allow you to go.
If you can apprise me about your problem earlier, I would have allowed you to go.
questions.solution_en: This is a conditional sentence expressing an unreal past condition (third conditional). The error is in the main clause where "allow" should be in past participle form as "allowed" since it follows the modal auxiliary "would have." The correct structure for third conditional sentences is: "If + past perfect, would/could/might + have + past participle." 1 correctly uses "had apprised" in the if-clause and "would have allowed" in the main clause.

questions.q_en:
Directions [Set of 5 Questions]:In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

The importance of geography __(A)__ just come from understanding the physical properties __(B)__ the world, although that is of course important in its own right. It also __(C)__ from how it connects people to their environment. The ability to understand __(D)__ connectedness makes geography an important part of education, of our understanding of the world around__(E)__, and our understanding of human history.

Which of the following words can replace the blank marked as (A) in the passage?
questions.solution_en:
The passage conveys that geography is important not only because it helps us understand physical properties but also to understand how people connect to the environment. The blank requires an auxiliary verb as there is already the main verb 'come' present in the sentence. Another point to note is that the context requires the blank to be filled with a negative auxiliary verb which eliminates options c) and d). Option a) can be eliminated because it is plural and does not agree with the singular subject 'importance'. Therefore, the correct answer is option b).

Note:

Subject-Verb Agreement: Matching up singular or plural subjects with singular or plural forms of a verb is part of the process called agreement. This can be understood better by the examples given: - "She likes cooking." [singular subject and verb] -- "They like to cook vegetables." [plural subject and verb]

A Verb is a word or group of words that is used to indicate that something happens or exists, for example, bring, happen, be, do.

Main verb is the principal verb in any sentence. It denotes an action or state of being. Main verbs can stand alone, or they can be used with a helping (auxiliary) verb.

Auxiliary verb: A verb that gives grammatical information that is not given by the main verb of a sentence. It supports the main verb. Auxiliary verbs help to form the various tenses, moods, and voices of other verbs. The principal ones are be, do, and have. Example: She will sing a song tomorrow. Here, 'will' is the auxiliary verb that supports the main verb 'sing'.

questions.q_en:
Select the word from the sentence below, which is an antonym for the word 'ambiguity'.

The contract was written with remarkable clarity to ensure that all parties fully understood their respective duties and financial obligations.
questions.solution_en:
"Ambiguity" is the quality of being open to more than one interpretation; inexactness. We are looking for its opposite.

a) fully - is an adverb meaning completely. It is not an antonym.

b) clarity - means the quality of being coherent and intelligible; the quality of being easy to see or hear. This is the direct opposite of "ambiguity."

c) remarkable - means worthy of attention. It is unrelated.

d) respective - means belonging or relating separately to each of two or more people or things. It is unrelated in meaning.

Hence, option (b) is the correct answer.
